uber-data-engineering-etl.content:
## Introduction

End-to-end ETL pipeline on GCP processing NYC TLC Uber trip data. Extracts raw CSV, validates and transforms into a star schema via Mage.ai, loads dimension and fact tables into BigQuery, and exposes a flat analytics table for Looker Studio dashboards. An optional dbt layer adds lineage, column-level tests, and derived metrics.

## Architecture

![Project Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/main/architecture.jpg)

## Technology Used

| Layer | Tool |
|-------|------|
| Orchestration | [Mage.ai](https://www.mage.ai/) |
| Schema validation | [Pandera](https://pandera.readthedocs.io/) |
| Data Warehouse | BigQuery (partitioned + clustered tables) |
| Analytics layer | dbt-bigquery |
| Object Storage | GCP Cloud Storage |
| Secret management | GCP Secret Manager (optional) |
| Visualization | Looker Studio |
| Compute | GCP Compute Instance / Docker |
| Language | Python 3.11, SQL |

## Dataset

NYC TLC Yellow Taxi Trip Records — 100 000 rows covering March 2016. Fields include pickup/dropoff timestamps and coordinates, passenger count, trip distance, fare breakdown, rate code, and payment type.

- Dataset: [data/uber_data.csv](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/data/uber_data.csv)
- Original source: https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
- Data dictionary: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/data_dictionary_trip_records_yellow.pdf

## Data Model

Star schema with one fact table and seven dimension tables.

![Data model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/main/data_model.jpeg)

| Table | Rows (approx) | Description |
|-------|--------------|-------------|
| `fact_table` | ~100k | One row per trip; FKs to all dims + fare fields. Partitioned by `tpep_pickup_datetime`, clustered by `VendorID / payment_type_id / rate_code_id` |
| `datetime_dim` | varies | Pickup/dropoff timestamps + extracted hour/day/month/year/weekday |
| `passenger_count_dim` | ~10 | Deduplicated passenger counts |
| `trip_distance_dim` | 4 | Bucketed distance ranges: 0-1 mi, 1-5 mi, 5-10 mi, 10+ mi |
| `rate_code_dim` | 6 | Rate code ID → name (Standard, JFK, Newark, etc.) |
| `pickup_location_dim` | varies | Pickup lat/lon pairs |
| `dropoff_location_dim` | varies | Dropoff lat/lon pairs |
| `payment_type_dim` | 6 | Payment type ID → name (Credit card, Cash, etc.) |

## Pipeline Scripts

| Stage | File | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| Extract | [mage-files/extract.py](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/mage-files/extract.py) | Loads CSV from GCS or local fallback; validates schema; raises on HTTP errors |
| Transform | [mage-files/transform.py](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/mage-files/transform.py) | Pandera input validation, data cleaning, star schema build, distance bucketing |
| Load | [mage-files/load.py](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/mage-files/load.py) | Exports dims (full replace) + fact_table (incremental append + dedup); partitioned/clustered BigQuery tables |
| Analytics SQL | [analytics_query.sql](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/analytics_query.sql) | Raw SQL flat table — superseded by dbt model |

## Data Quality

Transform stage enforces:

- Drop rows with nulls in key columns (timestamps, coordinates, passenger count, fare, total)
- `passenger_count > 0`
- `trip_distance >= 0`, `fare_amount >= 0`, `total_amount >= 0`
- Dropoff timestamp >= pickup timestamp
- `RatecodeID` and `payment_type` restricted to known valid sets (1–6)
- Pandera schema validates column dtypes before any transformation runs

## dbt Analytics Layer

Replaces the raw `analytics_query.sql` with a fully tested dbt model.

```
dbt/
├── dbt_project.yml
├── profiles.yml
└── models/
    ├── staging/schema.yml      # source declarations + not_null / unique tests on all raw tables
    └── marts/
        ├── tbl_analytics.sql   # flat model with trip_duration_minutes, tip_pct, cost_per_mile
        └── schema.yml          # column docs + accepted_values tests
```

Run dbt:

```bash
cd dbt
dbt deps
dbt run
dbt test
```

`tbl_analytics` adds derived columns on top of the raw fact/dim join:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pickup_date` | `DATE(tpep_pickup_datetime)` — partition key |
| `trip_duration_minutes` | Elapsed minutes pickup→dropoff |
| `distance_bucket` | Human-readable distance range |
| `tip_pct` | `tip_amount / fare_amount` |
| `cost_per_mile` | `total_amount / trip_distance` |

## Configuration

Set BigQuery target via kwargs in Mage or environment variables:

```bash
export BQ_PROJECT=your-gcp-project
export BQ_DATASET=your_dataset
# Optional: fetch project/dataset from Secret Manager instead
export SM_PROJECT=your-secret-manager-project
```

GCP credentials go in `io_config.yaml` (Mage standard) or via `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` for dbt.

## Incremental Loading

`fact_table` uses append + dedup strategy on `trip_id`:

1. New rows appended to partitioned BigQuery table
2. `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS (SELECT ... WHERE ROW_NUMBER() = 1)` deduplicates in-place
3. Dimension tables always full-replace (small, cheap)

## Running Locally

### With Docker

```bash
docker build -t uber-etl .
docker run -p 6789:6789 \
  -e BQ_PROJECT=your-project \
  -e BQ_DATASET=your_dataset \
  -e GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/creds/key.json \
  -v ~/.config/gcloud:/creds \
  uber-etl
```

### Without Docker

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
mage start uber-pipeline
# Open http://localhost:6789
# Add blocks from mage-files/ in order: extract → transform → load
```

Point `local_csv_path` kwargs in the extract block to `data/uber_data.csv` to skip the GCS download.

## Tests

Unit tests cover transform helpers and full integration — no Mage required:

```bash
pytest tests/ -v
```

Tests cover: data cleaning rules, FK integrity, distance bucketing (4 buckets), datetime extraction, location deduplication, and presence of `trip_id` in fact_table.

## Looker Studio Dashboard

See [looker_studio/dashboard_template.md](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/uber-data-engineering-etl-project/blob/main/looker_studio/dashboard_template.md) for:
- Recommended charts across 4 pages (overview, breakdown, revenue, efficiency)
- Calculated fields (`tip_pct_formatted`, `weekday_label`, etc.)
- Filter setup
- Instructions for sharing a reusable template

Connect Looker Studio to `tbl_analytics` in your BigQuery dataset.

bird-disease-classification-mlops.content:
> Production-grade end-to-end MLOps pipeline for chicken disease detection from fecal images.
> Transfer learning with **VGG16 / ResNet50 / EfficientNetB0 / MobileNetV2**, **FastAPI**, **MLflow**, **DVC**, **Grad-CAM**, **Evidently AI**, **Docker**, and **AWS ECR + EC2**.

[![CI/CD](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject/actions/workflows/cicd.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pankaj2k9/MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject/actions/workflows/cicd.yaml)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.8-blue)
![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-2.13-orange)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.104+-green)
![MLflow](https://img.shields.io/badge/MLflow-2.8+-blue)
![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-multi--stage-blue)

---

## Problem Statement

Coccidiosis is a parasitic intestinal disease in poultry caused by *Eimeria* protozoa, responsible for significant economic losses worldwide. Manual diagnosis from fecal images requires expert knowledge and cannot scale to large flocks. This system automates binary classification (**Healthy** vs **Coccidiosis**) using transfer learning with model-specific preprocessing and a full MLOps production pipeline.

---

## Dataset

**Chicken Fecal Images** — RGB photographs of chicken fecal matter for binary disease classification.

| | Coccidiosis | Healthy | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Total** | 195 | 195 | 390 |
| **Train (70%)** | 136 | 136 | 272 |
| **Val (15%)** | 29 | 29 | 58 |
| **Test (15%)** | 30 | 30 | 60 |

- Perfectly balanced classes (1:1 ratio) — no class weighting needed
- Fixed 70/15/15 split, `random.seed(42)` — bitwise reproducible across machines
- Source: private AWS S3 bucket (`chicken-data-for-classification`) — downloaded in Stage 1
- Input size: 224×224×3 (RGB), resized at preprocessing

---

## Model Performance (Test Set, n=60, seed=42)

| Model | Accuracy | F1 Macro | AUC-ROC | Params | Train Time |
|-------|----------|----------|---------|--------|------------|
| **MobileNetV2** | **98.3%** | **0.9833** | 0.9933 | 3.4M | 47.5s |
| **ResNet50** | **98.3%** | **0.9833** | 0.9900 | 25.6M | 153.0s |
| EfficientNetB0 | 96.7% | 0.9667 | **0.9978** | 5.3M | 58.8s |
| VGG16 | 91.7% | 0.9161 | 0.9678 | 138.4M | 347.7s |

> All models: frozen backbone, Adam lr=1e-4, EarlyStopping patience=7, 70/15/15 split, seed=42.
> Full results: `artifacts/model_comparison/results.json`

---

## System Architecture

```
AWS S3 (data.zip)
      │
      ▼
[Stage 1] Data Ingestion      → artifacts/data_ingestion/Chicken-fecal-images/
      │
      ▼
[Stage 2] Data Pipeline       → train/ val/ test/ (70/15/15 seeded split, seed=42)
      │
      ▼
[Stage 3] Model Training      → artifacts/training/{MODEL}_best.h5
      │                          MLflow run logged per model
      ▼
[Stage 4] Evaluation          → artifacts/evaluation/{MODEL}/metrics.json
      │                          confusion_matrix.png · roc_curve.png
      ▼
[Stage 5] Explainability      → artifacts/explainability/gradcam/{MODEL}/{class}/
      │                          Grad-CAM heatmap overlays
      ▼
[Stage 6] Model Comparison    → artifacts/model_comparison/comparison_results.json
      │                          MLflow parent run with nested child runs
      ▼
FastAPI Inference Service     → GET /  (web UI)
      │                          POST /predict  (base64 → label + confidence)
      │                          GET  /health   (liveness probe)
      │                          GET  /metrics  (latest eval metrics)
      │                          GET  /model/version
      │                          GET  /docs  (Swagger UI)
      ▼
Docker Image → AWS ECR → AWS EC2 (port 8080)
```

---

## Quick Start — Inference Only

Pre-trained model at `model/model.h5`. No retraining needed.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pankaj2k9/MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject.git
cd MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject

# Create and activate conda env (Python 3.11 + TF 2.15)
conda create -n cnnclassify311 python=3.11
conda activate cnnclassify311

pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt     # installs cnnClassifier package in editable mode

python -m uvicorn cnnClassifier.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
```

Open [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080) — upload a fecal image, click **Classify Image**.

API docs at [http://localhost:8080/docs](http://localhost:8080/docs) (Swagger UI).

---

## Full Local Setup — Training Pipeline

### 1. Clone & install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pankaj2k9/MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject.git
cd MLOpsE2EBirdDiseaseClassificationDeepLearningProject

conda create -n cnnclassify311 python=3.11
conda activate cnnclassify311

pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt     # includes -e . to install cnnClassifier package
```

### 2. Configure environment

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env`:

```env
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key_here
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key_here
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=mlruns
```

> AWS credentials only needed for Stage 1 (S3 download). Inference does not require them.

### 3. Run full pipeline (all 6 stages)

```bash
python main.py VGG16        # trains VGG16 through all stages
```

Or run each stage individually — **all commands from project root**:

```bash
# Stage 1: Download data from S3
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_01_data_ingestion

# Stage 2: Create 70/15/15 train/val/test split (seed=42)
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_02_data_pipeline

# Stage 3: Train a model (default VGG16)
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_03_model_trainer        # VGG16
MODEL_NAME=ResNet50 python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_03_model_trainer

# Stage 4: Evaluate on held-out test set
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_04_evaluation

# Stage 5: Generate Grad-CAM explanations
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_05_explainability

# Stage 6: Train + evaluate all 4 models, log to MLflow
python -m cnnClassifier.pipeline.stage_06_model_comparison
```

### 4. View MLflow experiments

```bash
MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE=true mlflow ui --backend-store-uri mlruns
# open http://localhost:5000
```

### 5. Run with DVC

```bash
dvc repro                   # re-runs only invalidated stages
dvc metrics show            # compare metrics across git commits
```

#### Local DVC remote (no AWS required)

```bash
# 1. Place data manually (skip S3)
mkdir -p artifacts/data_ingestion
# copy data.zip → artifacts/data_ingestion/data.zip
# extract   → artifacts/data_ingestion/Chicken-fecal-images/

# 2. Commit outputs to DVC cache
dvc commit

# 3. One-time setup — create local remote and push
mkdir ../dvc-storage
dvc remote add -d localremote ../dvc-storage
dvc push

# On a fresh clone (no AWS credentials needed)
dvc pull
dvc repro --downstream data_pipeline   # skips S3 data_ingestion stage
```

> The raw dataset (`Chicken-fecal-images`, 390 fecal images) is downloaded from private S3 during `stage_01_data_ingestion`.
> For fully offline testing, place `data.zip` and extracted `Chicken-fecal-images/` under `artifacts/data_ingestion/`, run `dvc commit`, then push to local remote.

> Switch back to S3 remote: `dvc remote default myS3remote`

### 6. View Evidently Drift Report

Run drift detection first (requires reference + current batch):

```bash
python -c "
from cnnClassifier.monitoring.drift_detector import DriftDetector
from cnnClassifier.config.configuration import ConfigurationManager
config = ConfigurationManager().get_monitoring_config()
detector = DriftDetector(config)
# detector.build_reference(ref_generator)   # run once after deployment
# detector.detect(current_generator)        # run periodically
"
```

Reports saved to `artifacts/monitoring/reports/drift_report_{timestamp}.html`

**Open locally:**

```bash
# macOS
open artifacts/monitoring/reports/$(ls -t artifacts/monitoring/reports/*.html | head -1)

# or any browser
python -m http.server 8888 --directory artifacts/monitoring/reports
# → http://localhost:8888
```

### 7. Start the API server

```bash
python -m uvicorn cnnClassifier.api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
# → http://localhost:8080       (web UI)
# → http://localhost:8080/docs  (Swagger UI)
```

---

## API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/` | Web UI (upload image, view prediction) |
| `POST` | `/predict` | `{"image": "<base64>"}` → `{label, confidence, class_probabilities}` |
| `GET` | `/health` | `{status, model_loaded, model_name, model_version}` |
| `GET` | `/metrics` | Latest evaluation metrics JSON |
| `GET` | `/model/version` | Model name and version |
| `GET` | `/docs` | Swagger UI |
| `GET` | `/redoc` | ReDoc UI |

### Example prediction request

```bash
# Encode image to base64
B64=$(base64 -i path/to/image.jpg)

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"image\": \"$B64\"}"
```

Response:
```json
{
  "prediction": {
    "label": "Coccidiosis",
    "confidence": 0.923,
    "class_probabilities": {"Coccidiosis": 0.923, "Healthy": 0.077}
  },
  "model_name": "VGG16",
  "model_version": "2.0.0"
}
```

## Production — AWS Deployment

### Required AWS services

- **ECR** — Docker image registry
- **EC2** — compute (Ubuntu, t2.medium or higher)

### IAM permissions

```
AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryFullAccess
AmazonEC2FullAccess
```

### GitHub Actions secrets

| Secret | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | IAM access key |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | IAM secret key |
| `AWS_REGION` | e.g. `us-east-1` |

| `ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME` | e.g. `bird-disease-classifier` |

### EC2 one-time setup

```bash
sudo apt-get update -y && sudo apt-get upgrade -y

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh get-docker.sh
sudo usermod -aG docker ubuntu
newgrp docker
```

Register EC2 as GitHub Actions self-hosted runner: **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner**.

### Manual ECR push (without CI/CD)

```bash
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <ECR_LOGIN_URI>

docker build --target runtime -t bird-disease-classifier .
docker tag bird-disease-classifier:latest <ECR_LOGIN_URI>/<REPO_NAME>:latest
docker push <ECR_LOGIN_URI>/<REPO_NAME>:latest
```

### CI/CD pipeline (auto-triggered on push to `main`)

```
push to main
    │
    ├─ [lint]     ruff check + black --check
    ├─ [security] bandit -r src/ -ll
    ├─ [test]     pytest + coverage upload to Codecov
    │
    ├─ [build]    docker build --target runtime → push to ECR
    │
    └─ [deploy]   EC2 self-hosted runner
                   └─ docker pull
                   └─ docker stop old container (|| true)
                   └─ docker run --restart unless-stopped -p 80:8080
                   └─ health-check wait (12 × 10s polls on /health)
```

## Troubleshooting

**`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cnnClassifier'`**
→ Run `pip install -e .` from project root. The `-e .` in `requirements.txt` does this automatically.

**`FileNotFoundError: config/config.yaml`**
→ All scripts must run from **project root**, not from inside `src/`.

**`model/model.h5` not found on API startup**
→ Either use pre-trained model in `model/` or after training: `cp artifacts/training/VGG16_final.h5 model/model.h5`

**AWS S3 download fails with 301/403**
→ Data ingestion auto-detects bucket region on redirect. Check IAM has `s3:GetObject` on the bucket.

**Slow training on M1/M2 Mac**
→ TF 2.13 uses legacy Keras optimizer automatically on Apple Silicon. Normal — training still works correctly.

---

## Original Contributions

The following are contributions built as part of this project:

1. **Backbone-specific preprocessing** — model-specific `preprocess_input` per backbone (VGG16, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0, MobileNetV2) matching each model's ImageNet training distribution
2. **Deterministic 70/15/15 split** — physical train/val/test directories, seeded, idempotent
3. **Multi-model comparison pipeline** — Stage 6 trains all 4 backbones under identical conditions
4. **Grad-CAM explainability** — full GradientTape implementation for all 4 backbones
5. **MLflow experiment tracking** — context-manager wrapper, nested runs, best-run retrieval
6. **Evidently drift monitoring** — embedding-based DataDrift + TargetDrift reports
7. **FastAPI migration** — 4 endpoints, Pydantic validation, singleton model state, startup lifecycle

````md
# CareSage — Medical Chat Assistant

CareSage is a lightweight **medical Q&A chatbot** built with **Flask + LangChain** and a **Pinecone vector index**.  
It supports **document-aware** answers (PDF/RAG) by embedding your knowledge base and retrieving the most relevant chunks for grounded responses.

> ⚠️ Disclaimer: This project is for educational/demo purposes and does **not** provide medical advice. For emergencies, contact local emergency services.

---

## Features

- **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)** with Pinecone
- **PDF ingestion** and chunking for knowledge base creation
- **Fast API-like Flask app** with a simple chat UI
- **Config via `.env`** (no secrets in code)
- **Docker + AWS CI/CD** ready

---

## Tech Stack

- **Python 3.11**
- **Flask**
- **LangChain**
- **OpenAI**
- **Pinecone**
- **sentence-transformers**
- **PyPDF**

---

## Project Structure (typical)

```txt
CareSage/
├─ app.py
├─ store_index.py
├─ requirements.txt
├─ templates/
│  └─ chat.html
├─ static/
│  └─ style.css
└─ .env            (create this locally)
````

---

## Prerequisites

* **Conda** installed (recommended) OR Python 3.11 available
* Pinecone account + API key
* OpenAI API key

---

## Local Setup

### 1) Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/<your-repo>.git
cd CareSage
```

### 2) Create and activate a conda environment (Python 3.11)

```bash
conda create -n caresage python=3.11 -y
conda activate caresage
```

### 3) Install dependencies

```bash
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 4) Create a `.env` file

Create a file named `.env` in the project root:

```ini
PINECONE_API_KEY="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
OPENAI_API_KEY="xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

### 5) Build the vector index (store embeddings in Pinecone)

```bash
python store_index.py
```

### 6) Run the app

```bash
python app.py
```

### 7) Open in browser

```txt
http://127.0.0.1:5000
```

---

## Notes / Troubleshooting

### Python version matters

Some dependencies require **Python >= 3.9** (recommended **3.11**). Verify:

```bash
python --version
pip --version
```

### Rebuilding the index

If you change PDFs or chunking settings, re-run:

```bash
python store_index.py
```

---

# AWS CI/CD Deployment (GitHub Actions + ECR + EC2)

This repo supports a standard workflow:

1. Build Docker image in GitHub Actions
2. Push image to **Amazon ECR**
3. EC2 (self-hosted runner) pulls and runs the container

---

## 1) Create an IAM user for deployment

Give the IAM user these policies:

* `AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryFullAccess`
* `AmazonEC2FullAccess`

You will need:

* `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
* `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`

---

## 2) Create an ECR repository

Create an ECR repo and save the URI, for example:

```txt
315865595366.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/caresage
```

---

## 3) Create an EC2 instance (Ubuntu)

* Launch an **Ubuntu** EC2 instance
* Ensure inbound rules allow your app port (e.g., `5000`) if you expose it publicly

---

## 4) Install Docker on EC2

```bash
sudo apt-get update -y
sudo apt-get upgrade -y

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh get-docker.sh

sudo usermod -aG docker ubuntu
newgrp docker
```

---

## 5) Configure EC2 as a self-hosted GitHub runner

In your GitHub repo:

* **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner**
* Choose OS and run the provided commands on EC2 (step-by-step)

---

## 6) Configure GitHub Secrets

Add these in:
**Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**

* `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
* `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
* `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
* `ECR_REPO` (example: `315865595366.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/caresage`)
* `PINECONE_API_KEY`
* `OPENAI_API_KEY`

---

## Security Best Practices

* Never commit `.env`
* Rotate keys if exposed
* Use IAM least-privilege policies (tighten later for production)

---

Used here. | | **Collaborative** | Recommends based on user-item interaction clusters. | | **Hybrid** | Combines both — used in production systems (Netflix, Spotify). | **Similarity metric:** Cosine similarity on TF-IDF feature vectors. n8n-integration-manager.content:
Step into the future of automation with our cutting-edge Workflow Manager. Designed as a proof-of-concept to demonstrate enterprise-level process automation, this project harnesses the power of N8N to simplify and optimize your internal workflows.

---

## Overview

This project transforms manual processes into dynamic, automated workflows using an intuitive graphical interface. With a focus on enterprise-grade reliability, our solution streamlines operations and elevates efficiency.

---

## Highlights

- **Dynamic Automation**: Convert routine tasks into automated, actionable nodes with N8N's intuitive interface.
- **Seamless Setup**: Utilize Docker Compose to effortlessly spin up Postgres, pgAdmin, and N8N containers.
- **Modular & Scalable**: Built with modern technologies to support growth and evolving business needs.

---

## Tech Stack

- **[TypeScript](http://www.typescriptlang.org/):** A statically typed superset of JavaScript, ensuring robust code quality.
- **[NodeJS](https://nodejs.org/en/):** Server-side runtime built on Google Chrome’s V8 engine, perfect for scalable applications.
- **[ngrok](https://ngrok.com/):** A reverse proxy that makes your local services accessible from anywhere.
- **[Express](https://expressjs.com/):** A minimal yet powerful framework for building web applications and APIs.
- **[Postgres](https://www.postgresql.org/):** A leading open-source relational database system.
- **[n8n](https://n8n.io/):** An open-source workflow automation tool that empowers creative process design.
- **[Docker](https://www.docker.com/):** Containerization platform that guarantees consistent development and production environments.

---

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

Ensure you have the following installed:
- **NodeJS**
- **Visual Studio Code** (or any preferred code editor)
- **Docker**
- **Git**

### Hardware Requirements

Developing and running the Workflow Manager involves simultaneous execution of various components (code editor, Express server, n8n, Docker, and Postgres). For smooth performance, consider the following specs:

| **Component** | **Minimum Requirements**        | **Recommended Setup**         |
|---------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Processor** | Core i5 (2-core, @2GHz)         | Core i7 (4-core, @2.5GHz)      |
| **RAM**       | 8GB                            | 16GB                          |
| **Storage**   | 128GB SSD                      | 128GB SSD                     |

### Project Setup

1. **Clone the Repository**
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/pankaj2k9/n8n-Integration-Manager.git
    ```

2. **Configure Environment Variables**
    - Create a `.env` file at the root of the project.
    - Populate it with the following entries:
      ```env
      POSTGRES_USER=
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD=
      POSTGRES_DB=n8n

      POSTGRES_NON_ROOT_USER=
      POSTGRES_NON_ROOT_PASSWORD=

      N8N_BASIC_AUTH_USER=
      N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=
      ```
    > **Security Note**: Avoid committing sensitive data to your version control. Use secure vaults or secret managers in production.

3. **Development Scripts**
    - **Start Development Mode**: Run `npm run dev` to launch the server in development mode.

---

## Running the Application

1. **Install ngrok Globally**
    ```bash
    npm install -g ngrok
    ```
2. **Authenticate ngrok**
    - Sign up at [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/), retrieve your auth token, then run:
      ```bash
      ngrok config add-authtoken <YOUR_TOKEN>
      ```
3. **Start Docker Containers**
    ```bash
    docker-compose up -d
    ```
4. **Install Dependencies**
    ```bash
    cd <project_folder> && npm install
    ```
5. **Launch Express Server**
    ```bash
    npm run dev
    ```
6. **Integrate Workflows**
    - Import the provided workflows from the `workflows` directory into your n8n dashboard.
7. **Configure ngrok URL**
    - Update the base URL with your current ngrok tunnel URL (displayed in your terminal).

---

## Access Points

- **n8n Dashboard**: [http://localhost:5678/](http://localhost:5678/)
- **pgAdmin Interface**: [http://localhost:5050/](http://localhost:5050/)
- **Express Application**:
  - Main: [http://localhost:8383](http://localhost:8383)
  - Health Check: [http://localhost:8383/api/healthcheck](http://localhost:8383/api/healthcheck)
  - The active ngrok URL will be provided in the terminal upon each server restart.
  
  ![ngrok Example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pankaj2k9/n8n-Integration-Manager/main/assets/ngrok.png)

---

## Contact & Support

For any questions or support, please reach out directly at [pkp2.me2k9@gmail.com](mailto:pkp2.me2k9@gmail.com).

npm install

yarn
